result:
All green: `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` reports 4 pass / 0 fail (the two new registration tests plus the existing starter tests).

**What I changed**

Registration now hands the welcome email to the queue instead of sending it inline. `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.ts` dispatches `SendWelcomeEmailJob` (`app/Jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts`, scaffolded with `guren make:job`) after the user is created and signed in — so a refused registration, whether by validation or a duplicate email, throws earlier and queues nothing — then redirects to `/dashboard` exactly as before. The job resolves the mail manager when it *runs* (global manager first, falling back to the app's configured one) and sends `WelcomeMail` (`app/Mail/WelcomeMail.ts`, from `guren make:mail`), which builds the subject `Welcome to <APP_NAME>, <name>!`, a plain-text greeting addressing the user by name, and an explicit `from` taken from `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`/`MAIL_FROM_NAME`. Neither the queue nor the mailer existed in the app before, so I added the two configuration layers this project structures such things with: `config/queue.ts` (drivers `sync`/`memory`/`redis`, default from `QUEUE_CONNECTION`, Redis client built lazily) and `config/mail.ts` (transports `log`/`memory`/`resend`/`smtp`, default from `MAIL_MAILER`, sender from the `MAIL_FROM_*` vars), plus `appName()` in `config/app.ts` so nothing hard-codes "Guren". `app/Providers/QueueProvider.ts` binds the queue manager, registers the job class so a worker can resolve it by name, and installs the default driver; `app/Providers/MailProvider.ts` binds and publishes the mail manager — both skip installation if a driver/manager is already present, so a worker process or a test that points the app at a holding queue and a recording transport keeps its own. Both are registered in `src/app.ts`. `tests/RegisterController.test.ts` drives the real app with `fakeQueue()`/`fakeMail()`: registering queues exactly one job and sends nothing, running a `Worker` over that queue delivers exactly one message with the expected recipient, subject, greeting and sender, and a refused registration leaves both empty. I also documented the optional SMTP vars in `.env.example`; `.env` itself needed no changes.
